title: Order checkout failing
executive_summary: INC-007 checkout failures are caused by a configuration change in order-service that lowered payment_client.timeout_ms from 3000 ms to 300 ms at 15:22Z (OPS-2375, config-bot). Starting at 15:23Z, order-service's calls to payment-service began timing out at 300 ms, error rate rose from ~0.6% to ~29-32%, and the payment-service circuit breaker opened. payment-service itself shows no error or latency regression; the payment team's "healthy" assessment is consistent with its own metrics.

hypotheses.description: Misconfigured payment client timeout (3000 -> 300 ms) in order-service causes premature timeouts on POST /v1/charges. Mechanism: At 15:22Z payment_client.timeout_ms was changed to 300. From 15:23Z, order-service logged PaymentClient timeouts after 300ms; timeout_rate went from 0.1% to ~35%, error_rate from 0.6% to ~30%, the payment circuit breaker opened (failure ratio 0.64), and retry budget was exhausted. Payment-service's p50 (~60ms) and p99 (~300ms) are unchanged, so a large share of calls that previously completed within the 3s budget now exceed 300ms.

root_cause_statement: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED (critic-approved; still an INFERENCE from evidence): configuration_regression in order-service - Misconfigured payment client timeout (3000 -> 300 ms) in order-service causes premature timeouts on POST /v1/charges.
corrective_actions: Revert payment_client.timeout_ms in order-service from 300 back to 3000 ms (OPS-2375), verify on all instances.
Once reverted, confirm the payment circuit breaker closes and error_rate returns to ~0.6%.
Retry or replay failed checkouts from the 15:23Z-revert window if the payment charges are idempotent-safe.
preventive_actions: Require review and a canary for timeout changes on payment-facing clients; reject changes that drop timeouts by more than 50% without a load test.
Add config validation bounds for payment_client.timeout_ms relative to payment-service p99 latency plus margin.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on order-service PaymentClient timeout rate > 2% and on the payment circuit breaker opening.
Alert on config changes to timeout keys in order-service.
Track order->payment client-side latency histograms, not only server-side payment latency.
limitations: Server-side payment metrics cannot fully explain a ~30% client timeout rate at a 300 ms threshold; the magnitude needs client-side traces to confirm.
Payment-service request_rate dropped ~14% from 15:37Z; cause unknown but likely downstream of order-service failures.
[agent-reported gap] No client-side latency histograms for order->payment calls
[agent-reported gap] Rollout scope of the config change across order-service instances not confirmed
[agent-reported gap] No historical incident search performed
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The checkout outage is best explained by the 15:22Z order-service config change that cut payment_client.timeout_ms from 3000 to 300 ms. The timing matches onset within about one minute, the log messages name the 300 ms timeout, and payment-service shows no internal regression. Revert the timeout to restore checkout.
